title: HPAC-ML: A Programming Model for Embedding ML Surrogates in Scientific Applications
problem: Integrating ML models into scientific applications remains a significant challenge despite ML surrogates' ability to approximate complex functions with low computational cost. The lack of easy-to-use integration mechanisms hinders widespread adoption of ML surrogates in modern scientific computing.
motivation: ML-based surrogates can substantially accelerate scientific applications by replacing computationally intensive components with faster model inference.
method: The authors propose a directive-based programming model enabling developers to describe ML model usage in scientific applications. The runtime system performs data assimilation using the original algorithm and can dynamically replace algorithm components with model inference. The approach is evaluated across five benchmarks testing over 5000 ML models.
key_novelty: A directive-based programming model with runtime support for seamless switching between original scientific algorithms and ML surrogate inference.
contributions: Directive-based programming model for integrating ML surrogates into scientific applications
Runtime system supporting data assimilation and dynamic algorithm replacement
Evaluation framework across five benchmarks with 5000+ ML models
Demonstration of up to 83.6x speedup with minimal accuracy loss (0.01 RMSE)
